whyText: Known for their blackgaze sound blending black metal and shoegaze. A popular band in the genre.
Pacific Northwest atmospheric black metal with dense, layered textures. Their Cascadian approach is documented at https://bandcamp.com/wittr and reviewed on https://rym.xyz/wittr.
French-German blackgaze project with lush, reverb-drenched post-black metal. Featured on https://metalinjection.net/lantlos and documented at https://rateyourmusic.com/lantlos.
Seminal death-doom act from Bradford, UK. Pioneered the genre with violin-led dirges. Extensively covered at https://encyclopaedia-metallum.com/mydyingbride.
Arkansas doom band with huge, melodic riffs and clean vocals over crushing tempos. Reviewed at https://pitchfork.com/pallbearer and https://sputnikmusic.com/pallbearer.
Finnish funeral doom pioneers with organs and glacial tempos. One of the slowest acts in metal. Documented at https://encyclopaedia-metallum.com/skepticism.
A band with unique sound and wide influences that many listeners enjoy.
Iconic drone doom duo known for extreme volume and extended compositions. Covered extensively at https://allmusic.com/sunno and https://thewire.co.uk/sunno.
Japanese funeral doom band releasing rare, private-press cassettes. Extreme in length and weight. Documented at https://discogs.com/corrupted and https://rateyourmusic.com/corrupted.
French sludge-drone duo with crushing riffs and harsh vocals, releasing limited vinyl runs. Featured at https://heavymetalmerch.com/monarch.
Japanese experimental rock trio spanning drone, noise, and stoner. Their drone works are covered at https://allmusic.com/boris and https://pitchfork.com/boris.
Chicago post-rock collective blending jazz, dub, and minimalism. Reviewed at https://pitchfork.com/tortoise and https://allmusic.com/tortoise.
German dark jazz quartet with funeral tempos, baritone saxophone, and noir atmosphere. Documented at https://discogs.com/bohren and https://lastfm.com/bohren.
Canadian post-rock collective with jazz and ambient influences, building from quiet passages to orchestral peaks. Reviewed at https://sputnikmusic.com/domakesaythink.
A band with unique sound and wide influences that many listeners enjoy.
Portland black-folk-metal band weaving acoustic folk and melancholic black metal. Covered at https://metalinjection.net/agalloch and https://encyclopaedia-metallum.com/agalloch.
UK neofolk act mixing Old English poetry with atmospheric folk metal. Documented at https://bandcamp.com/wolcensmen and https://encyclopaedia-metallum.com/wolcensmen.
Norwegian ritualistic folk project using traditional instruments and runic Norse texts. Very popular via the Vikings TV series. Documented at https://wardruna.com and https://spotify.com/wardruna.
Los Angeles noise rock trio known for abrasive textures and electronic-drum compositions. Documented at https://soundcloud.com/health and https://bandcamp.com/health.
Providence noise rock act with convulsive rhythms and angular post-hardcore riffs. Reviewed at https://pitchfork.com/daughters and https://sputnikmusic.com/daughters.
New York noise-rock institution spanning four decades and multiple reinventions. Covered at https://allmusic.com/swans and https://pitchfork.com/swans.
A Japanese artist with unique sound and wide influences.
Polish black metal duo with cold, minimalist riffing and bleak atmospheres. Widely discussed at https://encyclopaedia-metallum.com/mgla and https://rateyourmusic.com/mgla.
A black metal band known for their unique sound and their Orthodox liturgical influences.
Icelandic avant-garde black metal collective with ritualistic chaos and extremely limited distribution. Documented at https://encyclopaedia-metallum.com/hvileikaos.
